summary: N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran. He held positions at Deccan College (1960–1963) and the University of Madras (1964).

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy in the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh.

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) was a Romanian scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1909–1912) and the universities of Göttingen (~1913–1914) and Munich (~1915–1919), later teaching at the University of Bucharest (~1920–1938).
Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He succeeded Dalsukh Malvania as Acting Director at the L. D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctorates from Calcutta and London. He taught at Judson College (~1917–1920) and Calcutta (~1939–1958), later presiding over The Asiatic Society (1959–1961) and Maha Bodhi Society (1959–1973).

Nalini Balbir (born 1955) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at CNRS, INALCO, Sorbonne Nouvelle (from 1988), EPHE (from 2000), and serves as Vice President of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. Supervised by Leslie C. Orr, she completed a PhD at Concordia University (attested 2004) and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Helen Hardacre. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard and became a professor at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja (born 1974) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a doctorate at SOAS University of London and became Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary and the University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers including Mahasi Sayadaw and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami (1906–2002) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), where he later taught (~1948–1967), and served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including Kuse Serjong Shedra. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples, and founded the Shang Shung Institute in 1990.

Nancy E. Levine (born 1949) is a scholar in Tibetology and anthropology. She held appointments as Associate Professor (attested 1998) and Professor of Anthropology (attested 2026) at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Columbia University and completed a PhD at UC Berkeley. She holds a professorship at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Nancy Hock is an archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology scholar who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held an appointment at the Asian Art Museum (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson. She held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nancy S. Steinhardt (born 1954) is a scholar of East Asian art, archaeology, and sinology. She has served as a professor and museum curator at the University of Pennsylvania and its Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology since circa 1982.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Thubten Chökyi Dorje and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
